name: Stihl MS 170 / MS 180
blurb: Stihl's entry-level saws: 3/8″ Picco low-profile, .043″ gauge — 44 drive links on 12″, 50 on 14″, 55 on the stock 16″ bar (Stihl 61 PMM3).
intro: The MS 170 and MS 180 (including C-BE variants) are Stihl's lightest homeowner saws, sold with 12″, 14″ and — most commonly in recent years — 16″ bars. All use Stihl's Picco Micro Mini low-profile chain in .043″ gauge (61 PMM3): 44 drive links on a 12″ bar, 50 on a 14″ and 55 on a 16″. Stihl's own chain-selection charts (2017 and the 2025 catalog) list those three counts for one block of saws that also includes the MS 171, MS 180 C-BE and MS 181 C-BE, so the same loops fit all of them. The 16″ count is also confirmed by the OEM chain listing for part 3610 005 0055.

bars.note: Both STIHL charts list chain 61 PMM3 44 for this saw group; the recommended bar is 3005 008 3905 in the 2025 chart (3005 000 3905 in 2017).
Both STIHL charts list chain 61 PMM3 50 for this saw group; the recommended bar is 3005 008 3909 in the 2025 chart (3005 000 3909 in 2017).

The stock fitment for current MS 170 / MS 180 saws. Discontinued pre-2023 examples on the older .050″ Picco setup exist — if your stamp reads .050″ / 1.3 mm, your chain is the 63 PM3 type instead. STIHL's 2017 and 2025 chain charts list the same 61 PMM3 55 loop with bar 3005 008 3913.
